name: Sympathy
overview: The Scriptures reveal sympathy as a profound expression of compassionate presence and heartfelt mourning for those who suffer, as exemplified by Job's friends who came to comfort him and sat silently with him in his grief (Job 2:11-13). Genuine sympathy involves both emotional sharing and practical support, reflecting a godly fear and respect for the Almighty (Job 6:14). Moreover, the wise recognize the solemn reality of human mortality and are moved to empathy, understanding that such moments call for heartfelt reflection and encouragement (Ecclesiastes 7:2; Job 22:29).
